threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look baffled when the tube is on strike—locals just grab a bike or walk, and carry on like it's a sunny day.
Last night on the 133, a bloke serenaded the driver with an off-key rendition of 'Wonderwall' while everyone tried to ignore him. Pure Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I found my favorite kebab shop still open at 3 AM, with the owner sharing stories about every late-night customer.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you find techno parties in abandoned buildings that last all weekend, complete with makeshift bars and old couches to crash on.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a true local by their instinct to grab a burrito in hand, even if they’re late for BART; tourists just stare at the menu.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 31 at 5:15, driver stopped for a street performer doing backflips. Crowd laughed, he took a bow, then we all packed in like sardines.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists always ask for the best tapas bar, but they miss the tiny bodegas where locals actually grab a quick vermut. That's where the real vibe is.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a newbie by the way they stop at every crosswalk, waiting for the light, while locals just zip across without a second thought.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the market's a quick jaunt, not realizing you’ll need to navigate the endless queues and pop-up stalls for a good 45 minutes.
Caught a night bus from Brixton to Clapham, and there was a guy gleefully singing 'Wonderwall' while everyone pretended not to listen. Classic Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw a guy in a full tuxedo casually waiting for the bus next to someone in pajamas. Only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you grab a döner, then stroll to a hidden courtyard where artists hang their creations on the walls, almost like a gallery.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they instinctively avoid the 24th St. BART entrance during rush hour like it's a wildfire zone.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni at 9th and Market where a saxophonist played 'Take Five' while the bus was stuck behind a fire truck. Perfectly San Francisco.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often miss that most locals don’t dine out until 9 PM. The evening buzz starts late, and the real vibe unfolds after sunset.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their confused look when the metro doors close just inches from their hand, still clutching a map.
